text:
Maya: Following up from todays runtime Q&A  posting the live thread for kernel prewarm, microbatching knobs, and tenant isolation questions.
Ethan: Thanks. Two quick asks: exact ETA for per-tenant batch policy + will it be opt-in per route?
Maya: ETA: infra API in ~3 weeks, route-level opt-in via annotations in v1, Console toggle later as a beta.
Ravi: Any measurable tail impact from tenant isolation? Were worried about p99 for mixed workloads.
Clara: We did a tour-run on 8xA100: introducing micro-queues per-tenant increased p99 by ~6ms under sustained load, but reduced cross-tenant stalls and jitter for noisy tenants.
Zoe: Is the micro-queue approach compatible with our continuous batching engine?
Clara: Yes  we shard the batching window by tenant tag before packing. Continuous batcher still runs per-shard.
Ethan: For latency-critical tenants, recommended profile?
Ravi: Recommend: max_batch=6, max_wait_ms=8, prewarm=true, isolated_pool=true. Avoid min_batch>1.
Maya: Well publish a pasteable policy; Ops asked for a tiny example.
Ethan: Cool. Draft config useful: 

```
batch_policy: low_latency
max_batch: 6
max_wait_ms: 8
prewarm: enabled
pool: isolated
kv_cache_mode: shared
```

Ravi: Note about kv_cache_mode: shared vs isolated tradeoff: shared improves hit rate but risks noisy eviction; isolated costs memory.
Zoe: Kernel prewarm status? Cold CVS for long-context models still hurting first-token.
Clara: Kernel team landed a preheat worker prototype that does: compile-hot-paths, populate kv cache with predicted prefixes, and touch attention kernels. In our bench it cut first-token by ~45-80ms depending on model and quantization.
Maya: Important: prewarm will be configurable per-model and per-policy. We'll gate it behind a canary flag.
OpsBot: Canary rollout: kernel-prewarm v1 started at 1771234690, 5/6 nodes healthy.
Ethan: Any incompatibilities with q4_* kernels or CPU fallback?
Clara: Works with q4 and fp16. CPU fallback precompiles slower loops; it helps but delta smaller. We still need more test coverage for rare ops.
Ravi: Telemetry ask: can we get prewarm hit-rate, precompile time, and memory overhead in Console?
Maya: Yes  plan: add three metrics in the kernel panel: prewarm_hits, prewarm_time_ms, prewarm_rss_delta. Sampling in 10 days, full rollout in 5 weeks.
Ethan: If a kernel update regresses p99, what's the rollback plan?
Clara: Autoswitch: routing will revert to previous kernel binary for affected routes automatically if p99 delta > threshold for 5m. Also manual rollback via release manager. Ops runbook coming.
Ravi: Any SDK header changes? We prefer header flags rather than RPC changes.
Maya: No breaking RPCs. New controls are via request headers + infra annotations. SDKs will add helpers in next minor release.
Zoe: Customer testing: can we provide a private canary pool to a few pilot customers?
Maya: Yes  Dedicated will expose opt-in canary pools. DM me to be added.
OpsBot: Canary update 1771234890: 6/6 nodes healthy, observed avg first-token improvement -58ms on long-context tests.
Ethan: One more: cache TTL guidance? We saw OOMs with 2min TTL at scale.
Ravi: Default recommended TTL: 45-60s. If memory pressure high, autoscaler will lower TTL and we add a soft-oom signal to evict less-recent keys.
Maya: Great thread  Ill collect action items and owners. If you want early access to the canary, ping me.
Zoe: Thanks!
